message:
test(otp): drop interface coverage targets that aborted the mutation run

Naming `ProblemCoded` / `ProblemExtensions` in `#[UsesClass]` makes PHPUnit 11 warn
(an interface is not a coverage target), and Infection treats a warning in
its initial run as a failure, so no mutant ever ran.

Merge TASK-022: one-time codes delivered over email

A recipient declared OTP_EMAIL now receives a code through Notification,
enters it and proceeds; a re-send really sends and the failed-attempt
budget survives it. Issuance is ensure (returns the live code, sends
nothing) or mint (replaces it) behind one route; a missing discriminator
means ensure. BL-157 is closed.

docs(adr-0051): promote to Accepted, with section 2.3 narrowed

TASK-022 landed and every bar in section 5 is green: the port, its adapter,
the narrow Deptrac layer and the enumerated-exceptions comment each have a
test holding them. The promotion was reserved for the owner and is made now.

docs(tasks): split the SMS channel and channel selection out of TASK-023

TASK-023 bundled a paid transport, a new class of personal data and the
OTP that rides on both. Cut into separate records (TASK-030 and TASK-031)
so each can be built and reviewed on its own, as TASK-022 was.
Merge TASK-030 and TASK-031: the SMS channel and channel selection, split out of TASK-023

fix(session): answer the open route's status from the session row, not the declaration

`POST /api/v1/signing/session` derived `status` from whether the sender
declared an access gate, a fact that never changes, so a recipient who had
already passed the gate was still told to face it. It now reads the session.
Merge fix/session-status-and-grant-expiry: the open route's status and the grant countdown

feat(session): let a stranded signer ask to face the access gate again

A credential pair is minted once, at the gate, and the signer app keeps it
in sessionStorage, which iOS drops when a tab is backgrounded (ADR-0053).
A recipient who lost it can now ask to be asked again instead of needing
the sender to intervene.
Merge feat/access-grant-recovery: a stranded signer can ask to be asked again (ADR-0053)

feat(session): the descriptor names the access gate even once it is passed

Recovery runs against the access gate, but `method` names the method of
the gate currently open, which is null after the door. A client offering
recovery could not tell which control to render, so `access_gate` is now
published beside it.
Merge feat/descriptor-names-the-door: access_gate for recovery screens

feat(session): publish code_length so a code input is sized, not guessed

The signer app renders a segmented six-cell input and nothing published a
width. The descriptor now carries `code_length`. Also documents that the two
code-length constants are equal by coincidence (a length produced vs. a floor),
and that ACCESS_CREDENTIAL_LIFE has three copies, not two.

docs: sweep four claims left stale by this week's re-cut

BL-117 still said it was discharged by TASK-023, which stopped being true
when that record was re-scoped; the other surfaces carried similar leftovers.
Merge the post-re-cut documentation sweep

docs(adr-0054,task-032): a gate declares an ordered method list the signer can descend

Eleven decisions: a recipient's gate widens from one method to an ordered
list of code-delivering methods, with the signer allowed to fall back along
it. The Number field is corrected to say the claim is local until the branch
is pushed, and again once it was.

feat(notification): the GSM-7 cost model and the Twilio transport seam

The provider bills per segment, and the GSM-7 default alphabet carries some
Spanish letters but not others, so one ordinary sentence can cost two
segments. Adds the arithmetic that counts segments and the transport seam the
SMS channel will send through.

feat(notification): add DeliveryChannel::SMS and the channel behind it

The first transport that spends money on every call. ADR-0037 claimed that
adding a channel is one tagged service and no routing change; this is the
change that pays for it. The copy is fitted to a single billed segment.

feat(notification): persist the provider's own reference on a delivery

A delivery row only said SENT, which means no more than that the provider
accepted the request. Storing the provider's message id lets "did it go out?"
be answered. Also limits the transport to one POST per attempt, since the
bus retry already multiplies a paid call, and adds a test that the
container finds the SMS channel.

Merge TASK-030: the SMS delivery channel

DeliveryChannel::SMS with its adapter and a Twilio REST transport, a cost
model that counts billed segments, and the provider reference persisted on
each delivery. It is the first transport that costs money per call.

fix(notification): four defects found by an adversarial pass over TASK-030

None was reachable from a live path today. One was a rationale whose reason
was false in the branch it justified (OneTimeCodeDeliveryService sharing an
arm between EMAIL and SMS); the others are fixed in the same commit.
Merge the adversarial-review fixes for TASK-030

docs(task-030): close the record with status, deviations and two new deferrals

Status now names the branch, the commit and the stack the checks ran on.

feat(observability): give ADR-0009 part 6 an owner and unblock the signer's preflight

ADR-0009 is reconciled with what was built (stderr rather than stdout, and
the parts that predate ADR-0032/0033) and amended to adopt tracing with the
span egress gated. `SensitiveDataRedactor` becomes the code owner of the
mandatory redaction layer (BL-29), and the CORS preflight now allows the
Sentry trace headers. No SDK is installed yet.

Merge the TASK-030 record close

Status names the branch and commit and says plainly that two acceptance bars
are unmet: the sandbox tier has never run, and delivery needs a Twilio account
and a processor agreement.

docs(tasks): give TASK-031's OTP bypass an owner, cut tenant policy per purpose

Three records each described the OTP's channel bypass as someone else's.
TASK-031 now owns it, and the tenant channel policy is cut per purpose.
Merge the TASK-031 review

fix(docs): an unconfigured SMS deployment does not simply boot fine

That holds for dev and test, where SMS_DSN is null://null. In production the
variable is absent and the container compiles on the first request, so the
failure shows up there. ADR-0037 and the config comment now say so.
Merge the failure-mode correction for TASK-030

fix(docs): the meter is BL-166, not TASK-023

Comments said nothing counts a paid message until TASK-023 lands the meter.
TASK-023 only adds the call site against a port that records nothing; the
billing table is BL-166. The references now point there.
Merge the metering-gate correction

Merge origin/develop: backlog rows interleave, develop's win where they overlap

BL-168 was inserted after BL-167 here while develop gained BL-169 and
BL-170 in the same place; resolved as develop's rows plus ours, in id order.

build: install libphonenumber-lite and verify the property it was chosen for

TASK-023 relies on telling Spanish mobile from fixed-line numbers, so that a
landline declared for OTP_SMS is refused at authoring instead of being charged
and bounced by the provider. Checked against the installed package.

Merge origin/develop: ADR-0054, TASK-032 and BL-168 land under the local commits

Local develop had diverged by 3/6: the TASK-023 re-scope, its review merge and
the libphonenumber-lite install were unpushed while origin advanced. No conflicts.

Merge develop into the sentry branch: 18 commits of drift under the observability work

Only docs/adr/README.md was touched by both sides, in different regions.

Merge the observability boundary: ADR-0009 reconciled, redactor built

Groundwork the Sentry integration rests on; no SDK is installed yet.

feat(envelope,session,notification): recipient phone and method-named channel

TASK-023. A recipient can carry a phone number, OTP_SMS is declarable, and a
delivered code travels on the channel its authentication method names rather
than whatever the selector returned. Includes the column, the E.164
validation and the landline refusal at authoring.

Merge TASK-023: the recipient phone, and the channel a declared method names

A recipient can carry a phone number, OTP_SMS is declarable, and a delivered
code now travels on the channel its method names instead of whatever the
selector returned.

feat(envelope): publish the recipient phone on the envelope response, in the clear

`GET /api/v1/envelopes/{id}` now returns `phone` per recipient, whole, beside
the `email` it already returned whole; a partial measure on one and not the
other would be incoherent. This answers the personal-data question TASK-023
escalated. BL-172 is closed.
Merge BL-172: the recipient phone is published whole, like the address beside it

feat(observability): add the E.164 phone shape to the redaction catalog

The phone is stored in clear and its type carries the Pii marker, so context
redaction covers it wherever it travels as a value. This adds the text
pattern for where it appears inside free text (BL-171).

docs(adr-0009): gate span egress on wiring, not on existence

Section 4.1 raised the sample rate once the redaction layer existed with a
green corpus. That became true as soon as the redactor landed, yet nothing
calls it and SentryBeforeSend did not exist. The condition is now that an
egress sink routes through it.
Merge develop: BL-172 answered, the recipient phone now published

feat(envelope,session): a gate declares an ordered list of methods, not one

ADR-0054 sections 2.1 and 2.2, TASK-032. AccessGate and SigningGate widen from
a single method to an ordered, non-empty list, validated per member and
published. Adds `AuthMethod::deliversCode()`, the Envelope-side twin of
Session's check, so only code-delivering methods are accepted at authoring.

feat(observability): wire Sentry and put the redactor in the path of it

Installs the SDK and routes every event through the redaction layer, so the
layer has a caller. Also stops .env.dev from blanking a DSN set in .env.local:
Dotenv loads .env.dev after .env.local, so its empty SENTRY_DSN overwrote it.

fix(envelope,api): the nine findings from the persistence and contract checks

Both checks found real defects. The main one was a migration docblock
claiming a guarantee the schema does not give; the rest correct published
API descriptions that disagreed with what the endpoint emits.

fix(envelope): the array_is_list guard is narrower than its docblock said, twice

The integration test written for the guard failed against the prose it was
written from, was corrected, and failed again. Both narrowings are now stated
where the guard lives.

feat(session): the signer can move down the list, and the move sticks

A recipient whose delivered code never arrives had no lever except the
sender. Now they can select a later method, but only from the list the sender
declared (ADR-0054), and the choice is persisted on the session.

fix(envelope,docs): findings from validation, and realize ADR-0054 sections 5 and 6

Records the artifacts the ADR names, sweeps four surfaces that still described
"the declared method" as a single value, and adds the tests the validation
pass found missing. The ADR status stays Proposed until the last clause lands.

feat(envelope,session): presentation mode; free choice sends nothing until picked

ADR-0054 sections 2.4 and 2.5. A recipient is declared ESCALATION or
FREE_CHOICE at authoring and the value is frozen. Under free choice the
ceremony issues no code until the signer names a method. Also records three
backlog items this work surfaced for other repositories.
docs(adr-0054): Accepted, all eleven decisions exercised

Merge develop: the Sentry observability work under the ordered method list

Only docs/BACKLOG.md overlaps; both sides append rows and neither renumbers.

Merge TASK-032: a gate declares an ordered list, and the signer may move down it

ADR-0054 is Accepted with this merge. A recipient whose delivered code did not
arrive had no move of their own and ADR-0049 section 2.7 forbids the platform
from picking one for them; now the signer can step down the sender's list.

feat(api): publish the problem-code catalog, and fail the build on an unlisted code

98 of 149 error responses named no code. ADR-0025 made the bounded context own
the term so the edge lists none, which also meant a new code touched no
published document. The catalog is now generated and a new code breaks the
build until it is listed. Also drops a published claim about enum casing that
had outlived its reason and finishes the casing sweep beyond src/ and config/.

docs(adr-0055,task-033): name the party our ceremony never meets

The eCMR consignor is the integrator's own customer, authenticated in the
integrator's system, and will never open our link. The record now covers a
machine-driven ceremony (the platform sends the code, the person types it into
the integrator's screen), the counter that bounds it (BL-183), why a per-key
entitlement is not a precondition (BL-184), and a guard so a ceremony cannot
run over an envelope nobody could have read (BL-61).

feat(envelope): publish that a recipient opened their link and how they authenticated

The first open has always been recorded in session.signing_session.created_at
but had no way out. It now leaves Session as SIGNING_SESSION_STARTED and is
stored on the Envelope recipient row, so `GET /api/v1/envelopes/{id}` exposes
first_opened_at, authenticated_at and the access method used (TASK-034).
Merge TASK-034: the sender can tell a recipient who turned up from one who never did

docs(adr-0055,task-033): keep provenance apart from content, name what consent covers

The asserted address and browser string are carried but not in signerIp or
the signer browser field. The assertion may be the integrator's signed artifact. The
schema follows ADR-0019: a fixed-shape value flattens to typed columns. The
machine routes drop the session segment, since none is addressable there.

fix(session): a signed session says so before the credential, on both routes

`POST /signing/session` answered AUTH_PASSED for a COMPLETED session. The door
really was passed, so the field was right about a narrower question than its
name promised. The status now says COMPLETED first, so a client no longer
offers recovery to someone who already signed.

Merge ADR-0056: a signed session says so before the credential

A recipient who had already signed was answered AUTH_PASSED with no
credential, byte-for-byte the stranded-signer body that ADR-0053 defines
recovery for. The client offered recovery and every send then failed.

docs(adr-0056): state a property in the contract, not a navigation instruction

`outcome`'s published description told clients to route to a neutral screen
for an unknown value, which the first client could not do. Also records the
end-to-end validation, and sweeps INTEGRATOR_DELEGATED, renamed to
INTEGRATOR_ASSERTED to avoid confusion with RecipientOutcome::DELEGATED.

docs(adr-0055,bl-189): the limiter is a valve; the ceiling belongs to metering

One number cannot be both a safety valve and a commercial ceiling, so the
limiter is now declared the valve. The backlog row is renumbered BL-189 because
an uncommitted BL-183 existed in another checkout. Also notes that a recipient
declared with the delegated method would otherwise be emailed a working link,
and that the word DELEGATED already means the opposite in RecipientOutcome.

docs(task-034): there is no preprod environment, and the deploy warning is stronger for it

Infra has dev, test and prod only. The section also now separates the two
deploy failures: only the harmless one (an absent key read defensively)
degrades gracefully, not the dangerous one.

docs(bl-183): put the warning where the next author will trip over it

Nothing in src/ or any migration writes RecipientOutcome::DELEGATED or
SKIPPED, so whoever builds leg reassignment will be the first. The warning
now sits in the code, not only in the backlog.

docs(adr-0055,task-033): delegation authorises an act, it does not prove identity

The catalog lists doors a recipient passes at our threshold, and a delegated
recipient passes none, so it is not a catalog member. Also corrects the count
to thirteen declarable members, not fourteen: DIRECT_LINK is refused by both
constructors.

feat(notification): one delivered-code purpose per auth gate

AUTH_OTP served both gates of ADR-0049 section 2.1 and its copy always said
it was for signing, so a recipient still at the access gate, who has not seen
the document, was told to continue signing. Each gate now has its own purpose
and copy.
Merge feat/otp-copy-per-gate: one delivered-code purpose per auth gate

feat(notification): each gate's mail gets its own badge glyph and shade

The two mails arrive minutes apart, look alike and carry different codes.
A distinct badge answers "which one is this" at a glance. Also corrects 17
dates in the docs (the gate split landed on the 25th) and finishes the
AUTH_OTP sweep across ADR-0049, BL-164 and test docblocks.

docs(adr-0055,task-033): bind the assertion to the document that was signed

Every field in the assertion said who acted and when, none said over what, so
a signatory claiming to have authorised waybill 1 and not 2 met a record that
could not answer. A document hash is added.

Merge feat/recipient-access-trace: the deploy window loses the whole envelope read

Prose only, on top of the TASK-034 feature. There is no preprod environment,
and the two deploy failures are separated: only the harmless one degrades
gracefully.

Merge develop into docs/delegated-signature

The branch was 21 commits behind, and ADR-0056 (which section 2.16 and the
task's 3.11 build on) landed meanwhile.
Merge origin/develop into docs/delegated-signature

feat(session): the masked mail address no longer shows the signer's employer

MaskedDestination disclosed the whole domain as a recognition cue, which is
reasonable for a webmail provider but not for a company domain a link holder
could use to identify the employer. Each half of the masked destination now
keeps two anchors, enough to recognise one's own mailbox.

docs(adr-0055,task-033): align section 2.14 and four claims with the six-field shape

The assertion was re-cut from eight fields to six, and 2.14, which decides how
it is persisted, still described eight. Four other claims were made false by
the push and the merge.

fix(session): a signature requires an envelope a recipient could already have read

Nothing under Session asked what state the envelope was in. The mint issued
for any (envelope, recipient) pair, the open had no precondition, and the read
model branched only on the session. A link could therefore act on an envelope
that had never been sent. Now `sentAt` is checked (ADR-0058).

docs(adr-0057): claimable recipients, a slot that ships without an identity

Proposed. The eCMR consignee is not known when the waybill is sent, but
the roster closes at send. Records the decision, two backlog rows it surfaced
and the index edits, plus TASK-036 (the slot, the claim and its refusals)
and TASK-037, each scoped to a disjoint half of the ADR.

fix(session): close what the audit found around the guards

An adversarial audit of the previous commit found no exploitable defect; the
predicate, the monotonicity of sentAt, guard ordering and tenant isolation all
held. The fixes cover the smaller things it did find.
Merge origin/develop into fix/signature-requires-readable-envelope

test(envelope): lock sent_at through the write-side round trip

Corrects an overstated gap: the claim that no integration test asserts sentAt
came from a grep that missed the cases. Also sweeps three files the rotted-
reason pass left half-converted, promotes ADR-0058 to Accepted, and records
that the assertion count varies between 11460 and 11463 from run to run
rather than drifting.

Merge origin/develop into docs/delegated-signature

Conflict in docs/BACKLOG.md resolved by keeping both sides' rows.

docs(adr-0055,task-033,bl-184): the open question in 2.8 is answered, narrowly

ADR-0058 and TASK-035 landed, which made four claims across three documents
stale. A slot may be declared claimable and also signs, so the machine route
has to say so. BL-196 records that the actionable-recipient threshold was
crossed by a sum of three conditions.

docs(adr): what a dead envelope and a changed holder owe a live credential

ADR-0059 closes the terminal direction ADR-0058 section 2.6 handed forward.
A voided envelope stayed readable at four crossings, not the three BL-87
counts: the session open, under a neutral access gate, is the one no record
named.

docs(bl-195): the guard is in the right place, but the stated reason is false

ADR-0058 section 2.3 rejects the SigningTokenIssuer port because a storage
adapter cannot answer a cross-BC question. deptrac.yaml does grant
Session's infrastructure access to the Envelope contract. The decision stands,
the sentence does not.

test(session): make the issuer census prove its exemption reasons

ISSUER_CALLERS listed the minting sites ADR-0058 exempts, but the test threw
the justification away, so a row with a false trigger argument passed as well
as a true one. Each justification is now checked.

Merge origin/develop into docs/claimable-recipient

Three ADRs touch this branch's subject. ADR-0058 decided the mint seam that
ADR-0057 section 2.5 decides, so the controller now injects
SigningTokenIssuance rather than the port.

docs(adr-0057,task-037): six corrections the merge made necessary

Section 2.5's premise was false against the tree: MintSigningTokenController
has not minted unguarded since ADR-0058 routed it through SigningTokenIssuance,
which already refuses a null sentAt.

fix(session): a signing proof dies of its own expiry and of a fresh admission

consumeSigningChallengeFor() accepted any verified, unspent challenge at any
distance in time. ADR-0049 section 2.4 argues the proof survives its
verification, not its own deadline, and nothing enforced one.

Merge fix/signing-challenge-expiry-on-consume: a proof stops outliving its deadline

Discharges the expiry half of BL-159, open since the August security audit and
reached by the signer app on 2026-08-26. The transfer half stays open; BL-197
records the shape that would close the class.

docs(session): the client did need a change, and the docblock said it did not

The new refusal was documented as routing the signer to /auth in both cases,
concluding no signer change was needed. That was read off a table that is only
the last resort; the docblock now says what the client must do.

Merge fix/adr-0058-rationale: the guard is right, the reason given for it was false

ADR-0058 section 2.3's rejection of the port placement cites a layer that
cannot answer a cross-BC question, but Deptrac grants Session's infrastructure
access to the Envelope contract. The decision stands, the sentence is fixed.

Merge chore/issuer-census-pointers: the issuer census must now prove its exemption reasons

The census discarded each justification, so a false trigger argument passed
as well as a true one. Each row's reason is now checked.

Merge docs/claimable-recipient: a recipient slot that ships without an identity

ADR-0057 records the claimable slot, a party the sender cannot name when the
envelope is authored, declared as deliberately empty rather than inferred
from a missing contact. TASK-036 and TASK-037 split the work.

Merge docs/delegated-signature: the consignor who never opens the link

ADR-0055 records delegated signature, a party authenticated inside the
integrator's own system, as an authorisation to act rather than a way of
proving identity, with TASK-033 as its implementation record.

fix(event-log): the relay watermark survives a cluster restore

The cursor compares the transaction id first, which assumes
pg_current_xact_id() never goes backwards over the life of the data. A dump
and restore into a new cluster breaks that. Adds an epoch floor, a test for
the case where floor and restored cursor disagree (found by mutation testing),
and a check against a real dump and restore.

feat(task-038): a voided envelope closes the reads, not only the writes

TASK-021 asked whether the envelope is alive at the three ceremony acts but
never on a read. This closes the session open, the read model and the document
bytes; the renewal follows in the next commit.

feat(task-038): the void reaches the session row so the renewal can refuse without asking

The renewal reads nothing, and ADR-0058 section 2.6 exempted it deliberately.
But sentAt only moves in the safe direction, so a session opened legitimately
could renew forever after a void. The void now marks the session row.

feat(task-039): a credential stops working when the fact that justified it changes

Two sender gestures admit a live credential should die and neither revoked
it: a corrected contact (BL-152) left the old link working from the wrong
mailbox for its remaining seven days, and a similar case on the holder side.

docs(adr): the retention clock leaves the bucket, and the purge unit becomes the envelope

The WORM zones carry a five-year bucket-default retention that decides both
when bytes may be destroyed and when a document stops existing for the
customer. Fused, the second answer becomes five years, which conflicts with
the GDPR erasure right.
